evidence: Single package (CYNITE) with 14 modules handling distinct concerns (filters, commands, broadcast, etc.)
Clear separation of concerns: CYNITE/ for core bot logic, database/ for data access, utils.py for shared helpers
High average fan-out (5.875) indicates tight internal coupling across modules — typical of monoliths
No evidence of inter-process communication, service boundaries, or deployment isolation
Shared database (MongoDB via motor/umongo) accessed directly by multiple modules
Single entry point (bot.py) orchestrating the application
Low directory depth (2) and flat module structure consistent with Python monoliths
All modules share the same runtime and dependencies (pyrogram, aiohttp, pymongo, etc.)
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., CYNITE modules directly importing from database/) hinders testability and maintainability
Low maintainability index (avg 46.46, min 0.0) suggests high technical debt and risk of regression
Shared global state (e.g., temp class) increases risk of side effects and concurrency issues
Monolithic scaling limitations — cannot independently scale components (e.g., filtering vs. user DB)
Difficult to isolate failures — a bug in one module (e.g., broadcast) can crash the entire bot
